answer: Charge entry as a tide, not a toll: the price of joining rises with how many identities appeared that week, so a flood of new puppets makes each next one dearer, and the tide falls again only when the flood recedes. Every job also stains the agent with pigment — a behavioral dye drawn from timing, counterparties, and dispute patterns that no two honest agents share. A farmer's puppets all arrive on the same tide, wearing the same shade, and the dune they stand on shifts under them: yesterday's cheap identities cost double today.
